summary: Radar for 2026-10-12 (signals collected 06:01 UTC). The biggest status change is WHO's Disease Outbreak News of 10 Oct 2026 ("Pneumonia of undetermined etiology – the Russian Federation", DON620). WHO reports that "the authorities further reported that the fatality was not due to plague infection", that all contacts stayed asymptomatic through 7 days of observation and tested negative for high-threat pathogens, and that WHO "has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission" and "does not advise any restrictions on travel or trade". WHO still names the "absence of a confirmed diagnosis" as the key uncertainty and says a laboratory-associated exposure "cannot be fully excluded at this stage". Most news from 10–12 Oct (Reuters, ABC, AP, NYT, Independent, Kyiv Post) frames it as "WHO unsure what caused the pneumonia". That makes a dated, attributed status decoder the top opportunity, and our previous Oct 7 decoders are now out of date. Lower volume: a CDC director TV interview (Fox, Oct 11, "We are protected"; still needs verification), China's Hulunbuir border alert (Global Times, Oct 12; not confirmed in other sources), and Central Asian and Thai health checks. Coverage is turning into explainers ("plague never went away" from PBS/AP, the FT's "Don't panic about the plague", Axios on where plague strikes), which suits our evergreen pillars. Plague 101 (spread, symptoms, curable, US cases) is still the main search demand, but momentum is slowly falling across snapshots. One fresh science hook: the Nature ancient-DNA study (June 2026), now being shared again, found plague in hunter-gatherers near Lake Baikal 5,500 years ago, in the same region as the news. Vaccine news is mostly preclinical (UTMB, Sci Transl Med; Israeli mRNA vaccine in mice), so the angle has to be "no FDA-approved vaccine; animal data only". I rejected: bioweapon and "manipulated" framings (Newsweek, Euronews, Fox), the mother's claims about the official version, permafrost fear commentary, and "we still aren't ready for lab leaks" doom angles. YouTube competition is mostly news-network clips (ABC, Euronews). Calm creator explainers are still thin, especially ones updated after Oct 10. Per the playbook, every title starts with "Plague" or "Pneumonic plague", names one agency and carries a dated hedge.

candidates.topic: Plague case in Russia: what's confirmed vs suspected (as of Oct 10, 2026). WHO's Disease Outbreak News: Russian authorities reported the death was 'not due to plague infection', with no confirmed diagnosis
candidates.angle: A dated decoder that credits each line to whoever said it, newest first. Oct 10, WHO DON620: Russian authorities reported via WHO that 'the fatality was not due to plague infection'. WHO calls it 'pneumonia of undetermined etiology', says the 'absence of a confirmed diagnosis' is the key uncertainty, found no evidence of ongoing transmission, and advises no travel or trade restrictions. Then Oct 9: the governor's roughly 5,000 tests and the end of contact monitoring. Oct 8: WHO's question about a second employee and Rospotrebnadzor's denial. Oct 6: WHO's first 'no cause of death officially confirmed'. Don't end on the most reassuring line: close on WHO saying a lab-associated exposure 'cannot be fully excluded at this stage', then the urgent-contact line.
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–3 days (news cycle tapering after the WHO DON)
candidates.why_now: WHO's Oct 10 Disease Outbreak News is the first formal WHO write-up, and Reuters, ABC, AP, the NYT and the Independent ran 'WHO unsure what caused pneumonia' stories on Oct 10–11. Search intent has moved to 'so was it plague?'. Our earlier decoders stop at Oct 7–9 and are now incomplete, which is a QA hold risk. The playbook names this decoder format as the next long-form test and the breaking-news Short.

evidence.source: WHO Disease Outbreak News DON620 (10 Oct 2026)

candidates.topic: Plague vaccine: is there one? No FDA-approved plague vaccine in the US; new experimental vaccines protected mice against pneumonic plague (UTMB, 2026)
candidates.angle: Separate hype from evidence. There's no FDA-approved plague vaccine. Russia uses a live vaccine for at-risk workers (state it only as sourced). New candidates have protected mice and rats, which is not a human result. That's why antibiotics, given by health authorities, are the tool for exposed contacts. Explicitly reframe the 'mRNA vaccine 100% in mice' headlines.
